fullPassage: We often express problems interrogatively. Instead of commanding you to find my lost keys, I ask you, "Do you know where my keys are?" The question, in its surface form, seems to be a simple yes-or-no question about your knowledge, but you understand it as a request for help. Consider a common scenario: some feature of our domestic landscape goes wrong — the toilet keeps running, the drain gets clogged. Since there are possible things we could specify about the problem, we might wonder which description would be best. But as long as we can achieve the goal of getting the problem resolved, it doesn't matter precisely how we express the problem. We don't need to say, "The float and flapper of my toilet are out of alignment." We can simply say, "The toilet won't stop running." The goal is not to express the problem in its most technically correct form but to express it in a way that enables us to resolve the problem. Indeed, the best expression of a problem is one that also offers a tidy resolution.

② unusual: 드문, 특이한 — common의 반의어 ←정답
③ popular: 인기 있는 — 유사어
④ typical: 전형적인 — 유사어
det.tip: common scenario는 '흔한 상황'. 반의어는 unusual(드문, 특이한).

questions.passage:
(A) We often <u>express</u> problems interrogatively, asking questions instead of making commands.

(B) She boarded the <u>express</u> train to arrive at the station before noon.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 express의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) express는 '표현하다'라는 동사, (B) express는 '급행의'라는 형용사로 다의어 활용
det.analysis:
① (A) 표현하다 — (B) 급행의: (A)는 문제를 의문문으로 표현, (B)는 급행 열차 ←정답
② (A) 표현하다 — (B) 명확한: (B) 틀림, express train은 급행열차
③ (A) 배달하다 — (B) 급행의: (A) 틀림, 문맥상 '표현하다'
④ (A) 배달하다 — (B) 명확한: 둘 다 틀림
det.tip: express는 동사로 '표현하다', 형용사로 '급행의, 특급의'라는 다의어.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "arranged neatly and in order"

det.korean: 깔끔하게 정돈된 — arranged neatly and in order는 tidy의 영영 정의
det.analysis:
① massive: 거대한 — 무관
② crucial: 중요한 — 무관
③ messy: 지저분한 — 반의어
④ tidy: 깔끔한, 정돈된 — 영영 정의와 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: tidy = arranged neatly and in order. 본문에서 a tidy resolution(깔끔한 해결)으로 사용.

questions.passage: Instead of __________ (command) you to find my lost keys, I ask you, "Do you know where my keys are?"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 명령하는 — command의 동명사형으로 Instead of 뒤에 위치
det.analysis: command → commanding: 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사 형태가 필요. Instead of + V-ing 구문.
det.tip: Instead of + V-ing: '~하는 대신에'. command의 동명사형은 commanding.

questions.passage: But as long as we can achieve the goal of getting the problem __________ (resolve), it doesn't matter precisely how we express the problem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 해결된 — resolve의 과거분사형으로 get+O+p.p. 사역 구문
det.analysis: resolve → resolved: get + O + p.p. 구문에서 과거분사가 필요. 'getting the problem resolved'는 '문제를 해결시키다'.
det.tip: get + 목적어 + p.p.: 사역 구문. 문제가 해결'되는' 것이므로 수동의 의미로 과거분사 resolved.

questions.passage: We often express problems interrogatively. Instead of commanding you to find my lost keys, I ask you, "Do you know where my keys are?" The question, in its surface form, seems to be a simple yes-or-no question about your knowledge, but you understand it as __________. Consider a common scenario: some feature of our domestic landscape goes wrong — the toilet keeps running, the drain gets clogged. Since there are possible things we could specify about the problem, we might wonder which description would be best. But as long as we can achieve the goal of getting the problem resolved, it doesn't matter precisely how we express the problem. We don't need to say, "The float and flapper of my toilet are out of alignment." We can simply say, "The toilet won't stop running." The goal is not to express the problem in its most technically correct form but to express it in a way that enables us to resolve the problem. Indeed, the best expression of a problem is one that also offers a tidy resolution.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 도움 요청 — 질문을 도움의 요청으로 이해한다는 문맥과 일치
det.analysis:
① a form of criticism: 비판의 형태 — 문맥과 무관
② a request for help: 질문을 도움의 요청으로 이해한다 — 원문 그대로 ←정답
③ a test of intelligence: 지능 시험 — 문맥과 무관
④ an expression of anger: 분노의 표현 — 문맥과 무관
det.tip: you understand it as a request for help에서 질문이 도움 요청으로 이해된다는 맥락.

questions.passage: We often express problems interrogatively. Instead of commanding you to find my lost keys, I ask you, "Do you know where my keys are?" The question, in its surface form, seems to be a simple yes-or-no question about your knowledge, but you understand it as a request for help. Consider a common scenario: some feature of our domestic landscape goes wrong — the toilet keeps running, the drain gets clogged. Since there are possible things we could specify about the problem, we might wonder which description would be best. But as long as we can achieve the goal of getting the problem resolved, it doesn't matter precisely how we express the problem. We don't need to say, "The float and flapper of my toilet are out of alignment." We can simply say, "The toilet won't stop running." The goal is not to express the problem in its most technically correct form but to express it in a way that enables us to resolve the problem. Indeed, the best expression of a problem is one that also offers __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 깔끔한 해결책 — 가장 좋은 문제 표현은 깔끔한 해결책도 제시하는 것이라는 결론
det.analysis:
① a technical explanation: 기술적 설명 — 글은 오히려 기술적 정확성이 중요하지 않다고 함
② an emotional response: 감정적 반응 — 문맥과 무관
③ a detailed diagnosis: 상세한 진단 — 기술적 형태가 필요 없다는 논지와 반대
④ a tidy resolution: 가장 좋은 문제 표현은 깔끔한 해결책도 제시한다 — 원문 그대로 ←정답
det.tip: the best expression of a problem is one that also offers a tidy resolution. 글의 결론부에 해당.
